qa.q: How could reading books make people happier?
qa.a: Apparently, the more you read, the greater the perspective it gives you, and you start to appreciate what you have and what might be possible if you did things differently. That's especially true when you read the biographies of great people and realize the, well, great things you can accomplish.

qa.q: How might e-books make people read more?
qa.a: Uh, naturally, if they're smaller and take up less space, then you can carry them around more easily and so be more inclined to read them.

qa.q: What's the difference between e-books and paper books?
qa.a: Rather unsurprisingly, e-books are more portable and available in greater numbers. I think they're more accessible too for the vast majority of people, though if you're blind then you still might need something more specialist.

qa.q: Do people prefer e-books or paper books in your country?
qa.a: Quite surprisingly, most people seem to have stuck to regular books, though many have tried an e-reader at least once. I think it's down to the difference in experience and sense of accomplishment you get from physically getting through an actual thing.

qa.q: What can children learn from books?
qa.a: Same things as adults, though in a simplified format, presumably since they're younger and less sophisticated in their thinking. If you go to any school library you'll see there's a student with all kinds of books that cover everything, so it must be the case.

qa.q: And for example, so what exactly can children learn from books?
qa.a: Anything, like it could be hard to cook or it could be, well they've got like a simple recipe book, it could be hard to be a good friend if they see some examples in the stories they read. The sky is the limit pretty much.

qa.q: What's the difference between reading books and watching films?
qa.a: Well the sensory experience is undoubtedly very different. With books the action unfolds in your mind the way you understand it. With films it's unfolded for you in the way the director and others understand the material, though through sound and other parts of cinematography.

qa.q: What benefits does reading have for people?
qa.a: Generally it allows them to live the experiences and learn lessons from others in a condensed format. That's pretty cool when you think about it. So you save time. I suppose other positive things might include developing your imagination and vocabulary. There are loads of new and interesting words and concepts in books to learn about.

qa.q: How could reading books help people learn more about different cultures?
qa.a: Most obviously by raising their awareness of how other people live without having to actually visit the places. You could learn that through a documentary but books are more in-depth since they can be engaged with over a longer period.

qa.q: Do you think people will read more in the future?
qa.a: It depends on what you mean by more because if attention spans are getting shorter then they will not read texts which are as long but they might read the shorter texts more often than they read the longer ones now. So it depends on how you're defining your terms.
